clue.text: Couple with book about beast from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue the east is the right-hand end, so reading from there runs the word backwards
about means surrounding, so the word for book wraps around the other piece

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
a sow is a female pig

explanation.surface: A pair of people share a book about some creature from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: A twosome is a pair of people, which is exactly what a couple is.

clue.text: Pray for elevation of rank on vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word lifts it from bottom to top, so it reads upwards
in a down clue being on something means sitting above it

blocks.note: a rank is a line or row
a vessel is a boat

explanation.surface: Someone prays to be promoted while serving aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To worship is to pray to and adore, as a deity, so pray for in a devotional sense.

clue.text: Clever sting?

blocks.note: first meaning: quick-witted, bright
second meaning: as a verb, to feel a sharp pain

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a reading of a clever sting as a con trick; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for intelligence and also a verb for a burning, prickling pain.

clue.text: Dupes have stolen criminal's photo

blocks.note: mugs are gullible people
hot goods are stolen ones

explanation.surface: Swindled victims have had a crook's picture taken from them.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugshot is the police photograph taken of an arrested person's face.

clue.text: Cheerleader squeezed by composer in charge of a drunken revelry

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front
something squeezed by another is pressed inside it

blocks.note: J S Bach, the German composer
read as cheer + leader: the letter at the head of cheer
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A cheerleader is hemmed in by a composer who presides over a boozy party.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheerleader splits into cheer + leader: just its first letter goes inside BACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchic is the adjective from Bacchus, Roman god of wine, describing riotous drunken festivities.

clue.text: Term for antipodean with a worrying issue

indicators.note: worrying at something pulls it about, so its letters are disturbed

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian has a troubling problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Aussie is the informal name for an Australian, someone from the antipodes.

clue.text: Part of plant or insect found by bird  …

blocks.note: a corm is a swollen underground stem
taken as written
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A naturalist finds a piece of a plant or a bug near a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The cormorant is a large dark diving seabird.

clue.text: …  one returning to cold island in frozen water

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so it reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: I is the standard abbreviation for island
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
following on from the previous clue, one means a bird, here a diving waterbird

explanation.surface: Continuing from the bird, one flies back to a chilly island among the ice floes.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the cormorant clue, so one means a bird, the grebe.
explanation.definitionFit: An iceberg is a huge floating mass of ice, which is frozen water.

clue.text: Physician's advice is: "Do sort records out!"

indicators.note: sorting something out rearranges it into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A GP's instruction is to put the patient files in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctor's orders are the instructions a physician gives a patient, a fixed phrase for medical advice.

clue.text: Secretion from impure animal

indicators.note: the letters come out from inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs into the start of the second

explanation.surface: Some unpleasant discharge comes from a dirty creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is a compound excreted in urine, so it is a bodily secretion in a loose sense.

clue.text: Polish sign found in specialist word books

blocks.note: polish as a verb: to give a shine
a sign of the zodiac, the ram

explanation.surface: A shine and a star sign are located in some technical dictionaries.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish is capitalised only because it opens the clue; it is shine, not the nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossaries are lists explaining the terms of a particular subject, books of specialist vocabulary.

clue.text: Owlet's last to emerge from egg found in part of old roof

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: final letter of owlet
a chick hatches when it breaks out of its shell

explanation.surface: The final young owl to break out of its shell does so up in an old roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is straw or reeds layered as roofing, typical of old cottages, so it is part of an old roof.

clue.text: Made bespoke outfit for setter wearing tatty leotard

indicators.note: someone wearing clothes is inside them, so the setter goes within the garment's letters
something tatty is worn and messed about, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the setter refers to themself as I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A custom garment is made for the crossword compiler, who is wearing a shabby leotard.
explanation.walkthrough: The I is added to the letters of leotard before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that are tailored are cut to fit one person, which is what bespoke means.

clue.text: Unmarried ladies stress dancing round leg

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about and swap places
round means surrounding, so the jumbled letters enclose the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
pins is a slang word for legs

explanation.surface: Single women get anxious as they dance, perhaps around a leg injury.
explanation.definitionFit: Spinsters is the old-fashioned term for women who have never married.

clue.text: Remote and wild place of worship in Paris

indicators.note: something wild is out of control, so these letters run in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A church stands in some far-off untamed countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame is the great Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité in Paris.

clue.text: Relish old dance

blocks.note: a tang is a sharp flavour, something to relish
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a traditional dance.
explanation.walkthrough: Old dance looks like a single phrase, but old only supplies the O.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance that originated in Argentina.

clue.text: Water valves turned before engineer's first flood

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, read back to front
the first of a word is its opening letter
before means placed in front of what follows

blocks.note: taps control the flow of water
opening letter of engineer

explanation.surface: Taps are turned on before the engineer is first to notice a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a river in sudden flood, and by extension a sudden rush of anything.

clue.text: 23 wanting husband for countrywoman

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so something is taken away

blocks.note: the answer to 23 is a game bird, and this is a well-known example
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A game bird without a husband stands for a woman from the country.
explanation.walkthrough: The 23 is a cross-reference: an example of a game bird, minus its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a rural farm labourer, so a peasant woman is a countrywoman of humble status.

clue.text: Scot touring habitat listed to protect Buddhist's ultimate source of fragrant smoke

indicators.note: someone touring goes all the way round, so the Scot's name encloses the rest
to protect something is to shield it by surrounding it
the ultimate of a word is its very last letter

blocks.note: Jock is a nickname for a Scotsman
a Site of Special Scientific Interest, a protected habitat in the UK
final letter of Buddhist

explanation.surface: A Scotsman visits a protected nature site, bringing incense for a Buddhist.
explanation.walkthrough: An SSSI (Site of Special Scientific Interest) is a British conservation designation, which is why the setter calls it a listed habitat.
explanation.definitionFit: A joss stick is incense burned in Asian temples and homes, giving off scented smoke.

clue.text: Sherpas now mandated to carry a cold individual

indicators.note: the words carry the answer inside them, spanning their joins

blocks.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Mountain guides are required to haul a chilly climber.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowman is a figure built of snow, so quite literally a cold person.

clue.text: Carriage taking tea to free-for-all

blocks.note: cha or char is British slang for tea
a riot is a wild, disorderly brawl

explanation.surface: A coach brings tea to a brawling mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A chariot is a horse-drawn two-wheeled vehicle, a type of carriage.

clue.text: Endless talk about athletics event

indicators.note: something endless has had its end cut off, losing its last letter

blocks.note: to discuss is to talk about something

explanation.surface: People chat interminably about a sporting contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The discus is the field event in which a heavy disc is thrown.

clue.text: Creature shot by plucky woman?

blocks.note: game means brave and willing
bird is British slang for a woman

explanation.surface: An animal is gunned down by a brave lady.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: game birds are shot and then plucked of feathers, so plucky has a second sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A game bird, such as a pheasant or grouse, is one hunted for sport with guns.

clue.text: Trial of alternative way to give out cards

blocks.note: or introduces an alternative
dealing is handing out cards to players

explanation.surface: Someone trials a different method of dealing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordeal is a painful or testing experience, the sense of trial as hardship.

clue.text: Performing animal hosting "at home"

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the animal surrounds the other piece

blocks.note: a dog is an animal
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A trick animal throws an open house.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing means carrying out or performing an action.

clue.text: Stick with excellent source of claret to get a good drink

definitions.text: Stick with excellent source of claret to get a good drink

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

blocks.note: to jam is to stick fast
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 read as the letter I
opening letter of claret
taken as written
surface padding: it only qualifies the drink
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: Someone sticks with excellent claret in order to enjoy a decent drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a drink from the Caribbean that would serve well in place of the claret.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica rum is a dark, full-flavoured spirit from the Caribbean, regarded as a fine drink.

clue.text: Plant crowns of imported rhubarb in shrubbery

indicators.note: a crown sits on top, so each word gives only its topmost, first letter

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A gardener sets the heads of foreign rhubarb among the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: The iris is a flowering garden plant with sword-shaped leaves.

clue.text: Two articles sit uneasily with non-believer

indicators.note: something sitting uneasily shifts about, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a and the, the indefinite and definite articles
taken as written

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces sit awkwardly beside one written by an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: An atheist rejects belief in any god, so is a non-believer in the religious sense.

clue.text: Cook finally given opportunities to sleep with men on board

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

blocks.note: final letter of cook
nights are when people sleep

explanation.surface: A ship's cook is at last allowed some nights' rest along with the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: Men on board suggests sailors; the board is a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Knights are chess pieces, and chessmen are the men that sit on a board.
